title: Theranos: What the Jury Actually Decided
summary:
Theranos collapse explained from court and regulator records.
A jury convicted Elizabeth Holmes of defrauding investors, and acquitted her of defrauding patients. Using the Ninth Circuit's February 2025 opinion, the SEC's 2018 charges, the federal lab regulator's findings and reporting on the verdict and sentence, we show what the court record actually established: 12 tests on the Edison out of 300 developed, demos running a 'null protocol', drug-company logos added to reports, and a projected $230m profit against $1.94m of reported income.

Context: A24's documentary 'You Can See Everything' (Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim) about Holmes opens in US cinemas in October 2026. This episode is independent of the film and uses no footage, stills or quotes from it; it sticks to the court and regulator record.
sources: US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, United States v. Holmes & Balwani, Nos. 22-10312, 22-10338, opinion filed 24 Feb 2025: https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2025/02/24/22-10312.pdf
SEC press release 2018-41, 'Theranos, CEO Holmes, and Former President Balwani Charged With Massive Fraud' (14 Mar 2018): https://www.sec.gov/news/press-release/2018-41

ABA Journal, 'Jury finds blood-testing company Theranos CEO Holmes guilty of fraud' (Jan 2022): https://abajournal.com/news/article/jury-finds-blood-testing-company-theranos-ceo-holmes-guilty-of-fraud

CNBC via NBC, 'Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes sentenced to more than 11 years in prison' (18 Nov 2022): https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/business/money-report/former-theranos-ceo-elizabeth-holmes-sentenced-to-more-than-11-years-in-prison/3129509/

scenes.say: A United States appeals court has described the grandiose achievements touted by Elizabeth Holmes and her business partner as, in its words, half-truths and outright lies.

visual.text: The grandiose achievements touted by Holmes and Balwani were half-truths and outright lies.
visual.by: US Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit, Feb 2025
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Their company, Theranos, claimed it could run fast, accurate blood tests from a single drop. Private investors once valued it at nine billion dollars.

visual.label: Theranos's peak private valuation
visual.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.say: Yet when a jury weighed the evidence against Holmes, it did something many people still don't realise. It convicted her of defrauding investors, and acquitted her of defrauding patients.

visual.src: ABA Journal, 4 Jan 2022; Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: ABA Journal, 4 Jan 2022; Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: So what exactly did the court record establish? And why did the case that sent her to prison turn on investors, not on the people whose blood was tested?

visual.text: What did the jury actually decide?

scenes.say: Today we go through the paperwork: the indictment, the verdicts, the regulators' findings and the appeals court's opinion. And later, the one decision Theranos made that the trial judge treated as an admission.

visual.title: United States v. Holmes
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Chapter one. One tiny drop.
Holmes founded Theranos in 2003 and ran it as chief executive until 2018. The appeals court opened its opinion with the vision she sold: one tiny drop changes everything.

visual.by: The Theranos vision, quoted by the Ninth Circuit
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The idea was to replace the needle in the vein with a prick of the finger. Blood would go into tiny tubes called nanotainers, and be tested on Theranos's own miniature machine.

visual.title: The pitch
items: A fingerstick instead of a vein
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: That machine was called the Edison. Of all the devices Theranos developed under Holmes, the appeals court said it was the only one ever used to test patient samples.

visual.title: The Edison
lines: !The only Theranos device ever used to test patient samples
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In 2009, Ramesh 'Sunny' Balwani joined, later becoming president and chief operating officer. The court records that he and Holmes were in a romantic relationship from 2004 to 2016.

visual.text: Balwani joins; later President and COO
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Evidence at both trials showed Balwani oversaw the patient-testing lab and the deals with Safeway and Walgreens. But Holmes admitted that, as chief executive, ultimately all roads led to her.

visual.title: Who ran what
lines: !Holmes: 'ultimately all roads' led to her as CEO
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In 2010, Theranos partnered with Walgreens to test patients in its pharmacies. The public launch came in the autumn of 2013.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Now, the number that matters most. Theranos developed 300 small-sample tests while Holmes ran it. Only twelve were ever run on the Edison.

visual.title: Tests developed vs tests run on the Edison
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Other general chemistry tests ran on machines made by other manufacturers, some modified by Theranos. Holmes and Balwani pushed lab staff to move more tests onto the Edison, despite their concerns about its accuracy.

visual.title: Where the tests actually ran
items: Some of those machines modified by Theranos
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Chapter two. The demo room.
Former employees testified at both trials that the Edison consistently failed quality control checks and was unable to provide accurate results.

visual.header: Trial testimony, as summarised by the court
visual.title: The Edison in the lab
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: According to the court, they told Holmes and Balwani in real time. Those concerns were dismissed, or the blame was shifted away from the device.

visual.sub: Concerns dismissed, or blamed on something other than the device
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: One laboratory director, Dr Mark Pandori, testified that the failure rate of the controls on the Edisons was notably higher than on the equipment he was used to.

visual.text: ...failure rate of the controls on the Edisons was notably higher than what [he] would see on the assay equipment with which [he] had familiarity.
visual.by: Dr Mark Pandori's testimony, per the Ninth Circuit
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: He also raised proficiency testing, the regulatory check meant to be a neutral way to judge a test's quality. At Theranos, those checks ran on third-party machines, while real patient samples ran on Theranos devices.

visual.title: Proficiency testing
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Then there were the visitors. Employees testified that VIP guests, including investors, were shown into a room with an Edison or a minilab, and led to believe it was testing their blood.

visual.sub: Guests were led to believe it was running their blood
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In reality, the court said, the device was running a null protocol, while some of those samples were secretly run on third-party machines.

visual.title: The demo
lines: Some VIP samples run on third-party devices
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Several investors testified that Holmes and Balwani led them to believe Theranos ran its tests only on its own devices, and that the truth would have affected their decision to invest.

visual.title: What investors said they were told
items: Tests ran solely on Theranos devices
The truth would have changed their decision
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Chapter three. What investors were told.
After the Walgreens launch, Theranos sold new shares. Three investors bought in late 2013, and three more in 2014. Each purchase became a separate fraud count.

visual.text: Six investors buy shares; each becomes a count
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The indictment grouped the alleged misstatements into seven categories.

visual.title: Seven categories of alleged misstatement
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Start with the money. Theranos's corporate controller testified the company had no revenue in 2012 or 2013, and net losses of 57 million and 92 million dollars.

visual.title: Theranos net losses
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In November 2013, Balwani told Holmes the company was down to 15 million dollars in cash, while spending up to two million dollars a week. By our arithmetic, that is about seven weeks of money.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: What did investors see? One, Lisa Peterson, testified that the financial documents she received projected a profit of 230 million dollars by the end of 2015.

visual.label: Projected 2015 profit, shown to an investor
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Another, Brian Grossman, testified he was told Theranos had generated 200 million dollars of revenue from the Department of Defense.

visual.label: Revenue from the US military, as an investor said he was told
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: And the reality? In 2015, Theranos reported total income of about one point nine four million dollars to the US tax authorities.

visual.title: 2015: projected profit vs reported income
items: Total income reported to the IRS
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The Securities and Exchange Commission alleged something similar for 2014: a claim of more than 100 million dollars in revenue, against a little more than 100,000 dollars from operations.

visual.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.say: Then the military. Theranos did have a relationship with the Department of Defense, to explore using the Edison in combat settings. The appeals court said that never materialised.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: On a recorded investor call in December 2013, Holmes said Theranos had been doing a lot of work for special operations command, in the context of missions in remote areas.

visual.text: we have also been doing a lot of work for special operations command in the context of missions in remote areas
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: But General James Mattis testified that the device was never put into the field by the military, never installed on a medevac, and never used to treat service members on the battlefield.

visual.title: General Mattis's testimony
items: Never installed on a military medevac
Never used to treat troops on the battlefield
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Then the logos. A Pfizer representative testified that after 2008, Pfizer and Theranos had no meaningful business dealings.

visual.text: Pfizer: no meaningful dealings after this
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Yet Holmes admitted she personally put the logos of drug companies, including Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline and Schering-Plough, on reports with favourable conclusions about the Theranos device.

visual.title: The logos
lines: !Logos affixed by Holmes herself, she admitted
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In emails to Walgreens, she described those reports as the companies' independent validation. Their representatives testified they had neither validated the technology nor authorised their logos.

visual.title: What the drug companies said
items: Did not independently validate the technology
Did not authorise use of their logos
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: And Walgreens itself? Its representative testified that while investors heard the partnership was expanding, it was contracting, partly because so many blood draws were taken from the vein, not the finger.

visual.title: The partnership
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Chapter four. The regulators arrive.
In late 2015, news reporting revealed problems inside the Theranos lab. Around then, the federal agency that oversees testing laboratories carried out an unannounced inspection.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: That agency, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, concluded that deficiencies in the lab presented immediate jeopardy to patient health.

visual.header: CMS inspection report, per the court
visual.title: Findings
lines: Quality control failures on Edison and third-party devices
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In March 2016, Holmes hired a new laboratory director, Dr Kingshuk Das, to respond. His team went back through the Edison's quality-control data for 2014 and 2015.

visual.text: A new lab director looks back
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Their written assessment concluded there was a possible patient impact for every test reported from the lab's Edison instruments. Das testified he found the device unsuitable for clinical use.

visual.text: there [was] a possible patient impact for every test reported from the laboratory's TPS 3.5 [Edison] instruments
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: When he raised it, Das said, Holmes blamed laboratory control failures rather than the device. He found that explanation unsatisfying.

visual.sub: Das testified that Holmes blamed lab control failures; he found that unsatisfying
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Then came the decision we promised. Theranos voided all of its patient test results from the Edison.

visual.label: Edison patient test results voided
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Holmes argued it was a precaution that should not be used against her. The trial judge let the evidence in, and the appeals court found no abuse of discretion.

visual.title: The voiding fight
items: Appeals court: no abuse of discretion
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The appeals court said the trial judge reasonably concluded that voiding every Edison result was an admission by Theranos, and by extension Holmes, that the results were, and always had been, unreliable.

visual.text: the decision to void every single patient test result generated by the Edison is an admission by Theranos, and by extension Holmes, that the test results were, and always had been, unreliable
visual.by: Ninth Circuit, on the trial judge's reasoning
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In July 2016, Theranos disclosed the agency's sanctions: its Newark lab's certificate would be revoked, and Holmes would be barred from owning or operating a lab for two years.

visual.title: Newark lab
lines: Holmes barred from owning or operating a lab for two years
visual.src: MedCity News, 8 Jul 2016

scenes.src: MedCity News, 8 Jul 2016

scenes.say: In March 2018, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged Theranos, Holmes and Balwani with what it called a massive fraud, raising more than 700 million dollars from investors.

visual.label: Raised, in what the SEC called a massive fraud
visual.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.say: Holmes settled without admitting or denying the allegations. She agreed to a 500,000 dollar penalty, a ten-year bar as a public company officer or director, to return eighteen point nine million shares, and to give up voting control.

visual.title: Holmes's SEC settlement
visual.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.src: SEC press release 2018-41, Mar 2018

scenes.say: Chapter five. What the jury decided.

After a two and a half year investigation, a grand jury indicted Holmes and Balwani. The final indictment had two halves. The first alleged a conspiracy against investors from 2010 to 2015, plus six counts of wire fraud, one per investor.

visual.title: The investor half
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The second alleged a conspiracy against patients from 2013 to 2016, and four counts of wire fraud involving patients.

visual.title: The patient half
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Patients testified. One said a Theranos HIV test came back positive, but two later tests showed she was negative. Another said she received an incorrect result about her pregnancy.

visual.title: Patient testimony
items: HIV test positive; two later tests negative
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: The court tried the two separately, after Holmes made allegations of abuse by Balwani in their personal relationship. Holmes went first, in late 2021. Each trial lasted nearly four months.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: On the third of January 2022, after seven days of deliberation, the jury returned a split verdict.

visual.src: ABA Journal, 4 Jan 2022

scenes.src: ABA Journal, 4 Jan 2022

scenes.say: Guilty: the investor conspiracy, and wire fraud against the three investors who bought shares in 2014.

visual.title: Guilty
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Not guilty: the patient conspiracy, and the three remaining patient counts. Prosecutors had dropped the fourth. And on the three late-2013 investors, the jury could not agree.

visual.title: Not guilty, or no verdict
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In a separate trial in 2022, another jury convicted Balwani on all twelve counts, including every patient count.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Why the difference? A verdict doesn't give reasons, and we won't guess what jurors thought. The appeals court does record that evidence linked Balwani to sending the inaccurate results and to buying adverts for Theranos clinics in Arizona, and that Holmes's December 2013 investor call was not played at his trial.

visual.title: What the court records
lines: !Evidence linked Balwani to the inaccurate results
And to adverts for Theranos Wellness Centers in Arizona
Holmes's Dec 2013 call was not played at his trial
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Chapter six. Prison and appeal.
At sentencing, the judge found a loss of 120 million dollars and ten or more victims. That produced a guideline range of 135 to 168 months.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: On the eighteenth of November 2022, Holmes was sentenced to 135 months. Eleven years and three months.

visual.label: months in prison for Holmes
visual.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.say: In court, according to CNBC, Holmes told the judge she was devastated by her failings, and apologised to investors and patients.

visual.text: I am devastated by my failings.
visual.by: Holmes at sentencing, as reported by CNBC
visual.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.src: CNBC (via NBC), 18 Nov 2022

scenes.say: Balwani received 155 months. In May 2023, the court ordered the two of them, jointly, to pay 452 million dollars in restitution.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: That included 397 million dollars for twelve investors, and fifty four and a half million for two corporate victims: Safeway and Walgreens.

visual.title: Restitution, May 2023
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Both appealed. On the twenty-fourth of February 2025, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the convictions, the sentences and the restitution order.

visual.text: Ninth Circuit affirms convictions and sentences
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: It did accept part of one complaint: some testimony from three former lab directors amounted to expert opinion, without the usual checks on expert evidence.

visual.title: Partly right
lines: !Parts of lab directors' testimony were expert opinion
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: But it called the error harmless. All three would easily have qualified as experts. And for Dr Das, other employees described the same problems, and the technology was only one of many kinds of misrepresentation the government presented evidence of.

visual.title: Why it was harmless
items: All three would have qualified as experts
Technology was one of many alleged misstatements
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: It also said the trial judge should have considered whether the shares kept any value. Again, harmless: the investors could not sell them, so for restitution, their loss was everything they put in.

visual.label: of each investment counted for restitution
visual.sub: Investors were unable to sell their shares
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: One more twist. In March 2026, Holmes's sentence was cut by a year, under a 2023 change for people with no criminal history. The judge wrote that this did not diminish the enormity of her crimes.

visual.text: this sentence reduction does not diminish the enormity of Holmes's crimes
visual.src: Bloomberg Law, 26 Mar 2026

scenes.src: Bloomberg Law, 26 Mar 2026

scenes.say: Chapter seven. Our analysis.

So what did the jury actually decide? It did not convict Holmes of defrauding patients. It convicted her of defrauding investors, specifically the three who put money in during 2014, and of conspiring to do so.

visual.sub: Guilty of defrauding investors. Not guilty of defrauding patients.
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: That matters. The popular story of Theranos is about a machine that didn't work. The legal story, as we read it, is narrower: it is about what investors were told.

visual.sub: Popular: a machine that didn't work. Legal: what investors were told.

scenes.say: Look at the list of misstatements the appeals court described: finances, third-party machines, Walgreens, the military and the drug-company logos. It said the lab director's testimony about the technology was not essential to proving any of them.

visual.title: Claims the court said stood apart from the science
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: In other words, you didn't need to understand blood chemistry to follow the case. You needed to compare what investors were shown with the company's own records.

visual.text: Compare the pitch with the paperwork

scenes.say: Two hundred and thirty million dollars of projected profit, against under two million dollars of reported income. A military that never put the device into the field. Logos added by the chief executive herself.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.say: Our view: the patient side shows how hard it can be to turn bad test results into a fraud conviction against a chief executive. The investor side shows what becomes provable when the claims are written down.

visual.text: Harm is hard to prove. Words are not.

scenes.say: For founders, the lesson is not to stop dreaming. It is that every projection, every logo and every demo shown to an investor can become an exhibit.

visual.text: Every pitch is a potential exhibit

scenes.say: And for the rest of us, it is a reminder to ask the simplest question of any miracle machine: whose machine is actually running the test?

visual.text: Whose machine is running the test?

scenes.say: Every fact in this episode comes from the court record, the regulators and the reporting listed in the description, with each source on screen as we go.

visual.sub: Court opinion, SEC, and the reporting cited on screen

scenes.say: According to employee testimony, when VIP guests visited Theranos, the machine in front of them was running a null protocol.

visual.title: The demo
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: The machine ran a 'null protocol'

scenes.say: Employees testified that guests, including investors, were led to believe the device was testing their blood.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Guests thought it was testing their blood

scenes.say: In reality, the court said, some of those samples were secretly run on third-party machines.

visual.title: Where samples went
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Samples went to other machines

scenes.say: Investors testified that the truth would have affected their decision to invest. Holmes and Balwani were both convicted of defrauding investors. The full story is on our channel.

visual.sub: Investors said it would have changed their decision
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: It would have changed their decision

shorts.title: Holmes admitted she put Pfizer's logo on reports praising Theranos #Shorts
shorts.blurb: The pharma 'validation' reports in the Theranos case, from the appeals court's account of the evidence.

scenes.say: Elizabeth Holmes admitted she personally put drug companies' logos on reports praising the Theranos device.

visual.title: The logos
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Logos added by Holmes herself

scenes.say: They included Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline and Schering-Plough.

visual.title: Logos used
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Pfizer. GSK. Schering-Plough.

scenes.say: A Pfizer representative testified that after 2008, Pfizer and Theranos had no meaningful business dealings. Yet in emails to Walgreens, Holmes described the reports as the companies' independent validation.

visual.text: Pfizer: no meaningful dealings after this
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: No meaningful dealings after 2008

scenes.say: The companies testified they neither validated the technology nor authorised their logos. Investors saw the reports anyway. The full story is on our channel.

visual.title: The drug companies said
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: No validation. No permission.

shorts.title: Theranos projected $230m profit. It reported $1.94m income #Shorts
shorts.blurb: Theranos's projections versus its finances, from trial evidence described by the appeals court.

scenes.say: An investor testified that Theranos documents projected a profit of 230 million dollars by the end of 2015.

visual.label: Projected 2015 profit
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Projected: $230m profit

scenes.say: In 2015, Theranos reported total income of about one point nine four million dollars to the US tax authorities.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Reported: $1.94m income

scenes.say: Its controller testified it had no revenue in 2012 or 2013, and lost 57 million and 92 million dollars.

visual.title: Net losses
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Losses: $57m, then $92m

scenes.say: By November 2013, it had 15 million dollars in cash, and was spending up to two million a week. The full story is on our channel.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: $15m left. $2m a week.

shorts.title: Theranos told investors about military work. General Mattis testified otherwise #Shorts
shorts.blurb: Theranos and the US military, from the trial testimony described by the appeals court.

scenes.say: General James Mattis testified that the Theranos device was never put into the field by the military.

visual.title: General Mattis's testimony
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Never put into the field

scenes.say: Never installed on a medevac. Never used to treat troops on the battlefield.

visual.title: General Mattis's testimony
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Never on a medevac

scenes.say: Yet on a 2013 investor call, Elizabeth Holmes said Theranos had been doing a lot of work for special operations command.

visual.text: we have also been doing a lot of work for special operations command
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: What investors heard in 2013

scenes.say: One investor testified he was told Theranos had made 200 million dollars from the Department of Defense. The full story is on our channel.

visual.label: Military revenue an investor said he was told of
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: $200m claimed from the military

shorts.title: Theranos voided every patient result from its own blood-testing machine #Shorts
shorts.blurb: Why Theranos's decision to void its Edison results mattered in court.

scenes.say: Theranos voided all of its patient test results from its own Edison machine.

visual.label: Edison patient results voided
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Every Edison result: voided

scenes.say: Its own review found a possible patient impact for every test reported from those instruments.

visual.text: a possible patient impact for every test reported from the laboratory's TPS 3.5 [Edison] instruments
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: A possible impact on every test

scenes.say: Holmes argued the voiding was a precaution and should be kept from the jury. The judge let it in.

visual.title: The voiding fight
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: The judge let it in

scenes.say: The appeals court said the judge reasonably saw it as an admission that the results had always been unreliable. The full story is on our channel.

visual.sub: That the results were, and always had been, unreliable
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Always unreliable

shorts.title: An appeals court called the Theranos claims 'half-truths and outright lies' #Shorts
shorts.blurb: What the court record says about Theranos, ahead of our full episode on Saturday.

scenes.say: A US appeals court described the claims made for Theranos as half-truths and outright lies.

visual.text: The grandiose achievements touted by Holmes and Balwani were half-truths and outright lies.
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: 'Half-truths and outright lies'

scenes.say: In February 2025, it upheld the fraud convictions of Elizabeth Holmes and Sunny Balwani.

visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Convictions upheld

scenes.say: It also upheld a joint restitution order of 452 million dollars. And it wrote that drug companies never validated the technology, as Holmes and Balwani had told investors.

visual.label: Joint restitution
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: $452m restitution

scenes.say: The device, the appeals court wrote, failed to deliver faster and more accurate results than conventional technology. The full story is on our channel.

visual.sub: How the appeals court described the Theranos device
visual.src: Ninth Circuit, US v. Holmes, Feb 2025

scenes.caption: Not faster. Not more accurate.
